title: Priest (1993) rigid block on a plane, water-filled crack

meta.title: Priest (1993) rigid block on a plane, water-filled crack
meta.notes: Priest's example 8.1 as two commercial programs model it: a 30 m face with the crest at x = 17.0 (60.46°, Priest's is 60° with the crest at 17.32, see V080), a 30° plane from the toe, a vertical 15 m tension crack holding 3.75 m of water, and a water table rising from the toe to 3.75 m above the plane at the crack, which gives Priest's linear pressure along the plane.

checks.published_by: Commercial program A, commercial program C, Priest
Commercial program A, commercial program C, Priest

source.reference: Priest, S.D. (1993). Discontinuity Analysis for Rock Engineering. Chapman & Hall, London; example 8.1, pp. 224–225.
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V079 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Priest's corners A (0, 0), B (17.32, 30), C (25.98, 30), D (25.98, 15); G = 8119 kN, U = 551 kN, V = 68.9 kN, F = 1.049 by his eq. 8.10 (γw = 9.8 in his solution; docs/kallor/priest-1993.md). The programs' crest at x = 17.0 makes the face 60.46° and the crack 8.98 m behind the crest, 1.5 % more block weight: cSlope 1.0483 here against 1.0490 on Priest's geometry (V080), where the programs also give 1.049.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
grieta de tracción: profundidad 15 m, fracción de agua 0.25 (cSlope tensionCrackDepth y tensionCrackWater); en ogs es `analysis.tension_crack {depth, water_fill}` (F5.2).
